canonical_statement: There is a smooth complex-valued first-order linear partial differential operator on R^3 and a smooth right-hand side for which the equation Lu = f has no local solution near the origin (in the regularity class specified by Lewy's theorem).
domain_and_universes: Provisional: complex-valued smooth functions/distributions on open neighborhoods in Real^3; exact regularity and neighborhood quantifiers await primary-source transcription
quantifiers: an explicitly specified smooth first-order complex linear differential operator L
an explicitly specified smooth right-hand side f
every sufficiently small neighborhood U of the origin
candidate local solutions u in the source-specified regularity class
hypotheses: L and f are the explicit objects in Lewy's 1957 construction
the equation and derivatives are interpreted in the source-specified classical or distributional sense
conclusion: No qualifying u solves L u = f locally near the origin.

alternate_encodings.target: non-surjectivity of L on germs at the origin
failure of local solvability for a smooth first-order linear PDE

excluded_degenerate_cases: The claim is not that every linear PDE is nonsolvable, nor merely that a particular boundary-value problem lacks a solution. Coefficient signs, complex conjugation conventions, the right-hand side, regularity, and locality may not be changed without a checked transport.
